title: More than one condition: SUMIFS and COUNTIFS
summary: Add up quantities and count orders that meet two or more conditions at the same time.
intro:
`SUMIFS` and `COUNTIFS` accept more than one condition, and only count the rows that meet every condition at once.

In `SUMIFS` the range to add comes first, followed by pairs of a range and a condition. `COUNTIFS` is made of range and condition pairs only.

faq.q: How does the order differ between `SUMIF` and `SUMIFS`?
faq.a: In `SUMIF` the range to add comes last; in `SUMIFS` it comes first.

faq.q: Can I use `SUMIFS` with a single condition?
faq.a: Yes, and it gives the same result as `SUMIF`.

sumifs-worked-example.prompt: `SUMIFS` adds up with more than one condition. Its first argument is the range to add, followed by pairs of a range and a condition. In `G2`, type the formula `=SUMIFS(D2:D7,B2:B7,"North",C2:C7,"Pen")`.

sumifs-notebooks-south.prompt: In `G3`, write the total quantity of notebooks in the South region.

countifs-worked-example.prompt: `COUNTIFS` counts the rows that meet every condition. In `G4`, write a formula that counts Youssef's orders in the North region.

countifs-with-operator.prompt: In `G5`, write a formula that counts the orders of 25 or more in the North region.

one-condition.prompt: In `G6`, write the total of all of Salma's quantities. One condition is enough here.

sum-range-position.prompt: Where does the range to add go in `SUMIFS`?
sum-range-position.hint: In `SUMIF` the range to add comes last, but in `SUMIFS` it comes first.
